```{ojs}
//| output: false
// VM is the shared utility library, loaded globally via _includes/head-scripts.html (js/**). This hero uses VM.plotting.config.
VM = window.VM
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// A fixed, non-editable decorative curve -- unlike every method page's
// plotter, nothing here is user input, so this skips the expression
// parser and math.js entirely and just samples plain JS closures. A
// Lissajous figure traces out a closed loop that's visually busy enough to
// read as "a live simulation" at a glance, and cheap enough to resample
// every frame with no caching.
// A closure over _plotDiv, called (not referenced bare) from the display
// cell below as heroPlot() -- matching every other page's mainPlot(setup)
// convention. A bare `heroPlot` reference, without the call, renders as
// Observable's generic object inspector instead of embedding the DOM node
// (verified the hard way: it dumped the div's internal Plotly properties
// as inspectable object keys instead of showing the chart).
heroPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  const SAMPLES = 720
  const ts = []
  const xs = []
  const ys = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= SAMPLES; i++) {
    const t = (i / SAMPLES) * 2 * Math.PI
    ts.push(t)
    xs.push(Math.sin(3 * t))
    ys.push(Math.sin(4 * t))
  }

  const layout = {
    margin: {l: 0, r: 0, t: 0, b: 0},
    xaxis: {visible: false, range: [-1.2, 1.2], fixedrange: true},
    yaxis: {visible: false, range: [-1.2, 1.2], scaleanchor: "x", scaleratio: 1, fixedrange: true},
    showlegend: false,
    paper_bgcolor: "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor: "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    hovermode: false
  }
  const config = VM.plotting.config({staticPlot: true, displayModeBar: false})

  return () => {
    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "vm-hero-plot"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, [
        {x: xs, y: ys, type: "scatter", mode: "lines", line: {color: "#8ab4ff", width: 2.5, shape: "spline"}, opacity: 0.85},
        {x: [xs[0]], y: [ys[0]], type: "scatter", mode: "markers", marker: {color: "#f87171", size: 11, line: {color: "#171b29", width: 2}}}
      ], layout, config)

      // _plotDiv is created detached (document.createElement, not yet in
      // the page), so it measures 0x0 at the moment newPlot runs --
      // Plotly's autosize falls back to its hardcoded 700x450 default
      // instead of the real (947-ish px wide) container, which left the
      // curve sitting left-aligned instead of centered/filling the hero
      // panel. Every mainPlot cell on the site works around exactly this
      // with the same ResizeObserver once the div is actually attached and
      // has a real size.
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)

      // Advances the marker one sample per tick and keeps it running for
      // the life of the page -- this cell has no reactive inputs, so it
      // only ever runs once, and the interval is what keeps the curve
      // moving after that.
      let frame = 0
      setInterval(() => {
        frame = (frame + 1) % (SAMPLES + 1)
        Plotly.restyle(_plotDiv, {x: [[xs[frame]]], y: [[ys[frame]]]}, [1])
      }, 30)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

::: {.vm-hero}
<div class="vm-hero-plot-wrap">
```{ojs}
heroPlot()
```
</div>
